criteria.error_taxonomy: Each verification fault gets its own domain failure (malformed token, stale token, foreign session) so application code can react per cause.
criteria.false_all: One false covers all faults: bad tokens, lapsed tokens, foreign sessions, empty credentials and illegal durations alike.
criteria.false_vs_config: Token faults (malformed, stale, foreign session or secret) answer false; only broken configuration (blank secret, blank session, illegal durations) raises domain errors.

csrf_failure.instructions: Which failure shape should CSRF verification use?

criteria.all_pairs: A lookup yields the complete wire-ordered list of pairs for the name and leaves selection to the caller.
criteria.first_wins: A lookup yields the earliest pair for the name, following the native getter, with the complete wire-ordered list still exposed.
criteria.last_wins: A lookup yields the latest pair for the name, letting trailing pairs supersede leading ones.

duplicates.instructions: For a repeated request-cookie name, which pair should lookup hand back?

criteria.adapter_enforces: Before serializing, the adapter refuses prefix breaches (__Host- missing Secure with Path=/ and no Domain; __Secure- missing Secure) and SameSite=None missing Secure, using domain errors.
criteria.enforce_prefix_only: Prefix rules derived from the name are enforced in the adapter; SameSite pairs flow to native serialization unchecked.
criteria.serialize_native: Everything the native constructor takes is serialized; browser handling is documented and the adapter adds no policy.

policy.instructions: Where should cookie prefix and SameSite policy live?

criteria.default_secret: Omitting the secret falls back to the native per-thread default that does not survive restarts.
criteria.explicit_required: Secret and nonempty session id are mandatory on every call and no fallback exists.
criteria.secret_handle: Raw secret strings never cross the boundary; callers pass opaque issued secret handles as with crypto keys.

secret.instructions: How should callers supply CSRF secrets and sessions?
